Mitsubishi Chemical Advanced Materials UK Ltd.
Job Description:
Mitsubishi Chemical Advanced Materials, a group company of Mitsubishi Chemical Group is a leading global manufacturer of high-performance thermoplastic materials. We are continuously developing new areas of applications in close cooperation with industry leaders in a broad variety of customer markets.
Todmorden Site
At our Todmorden site, we specialise in engineering high-quality plastic parts and shapes for a wide range of industries - from everyday essentials like high chairs and swimming pool grates to advanced components for the aerospace sector.
We’re a close-knit team of over 30 dedicated professionals who take pride in our friendly, supportive work environment. Health, well-being, and safety are at the heart of everything we do - and we’re proud to say we’ve maintained a spotless safety record for over 15 years.

• Operate a range of specialist plastics equipment to produce machined components within precise drawing tolerances.
• Liaise with the planner to ensure machined components consistently meet drawing specifications and tolerances, always maintaining high quality standards.
• Support secondary operations, ensuring all dispatches are packed to maintain our high-quality standards.
• Assist with planning and production of customer parts.
• Support warehouse duties, including handling materials, preparing shipments, and maintaining stock accuracy.
• Carry out set tasks in a safe, efficient, and timely manner.

• A proactive team player with a strong work ethic.
• Someone who values safety, precision, and quality.

• Pension contribution matched plus increased % contribution from the company (the percentage increase from the company depends on the employee contribution).

• Health Cash Plan (claim money back on everyday health needs such as dentist, opticians, chiropractors etc.)
• Employee Assistance Programme.
• Free car parking.
• A friendly, safe place to work with a focus on safety.
What Could You Expect?
Our corporate culture is based on the values of integrity, respect, bravery, collaboration, and persistence, we call it "Our Way". With our approach, together we can shape a more sustainable, progressive and brighter version of the world.
We believe in the power of people with diverse values, viewpoints, and expertise. Our aim is the wellbeing of people and the planet – a concept we call KAITEKI.  We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment.

Job Description:
Start date: September 2027
Location: Filton, Bristol
Duration: 4 years
University: Weston College
Qualification: Engineering Manufacturing Technician Level 4 qualification
Application closing date: Applications will be open until 26 October 2026. After this date, the advert will close once sufficient applications are received. Early submission is recommended.
We love your interest in joining Airbus! There is no limit on the number of positions you can apply for. However, please be aware that you can only progress in the selection process for one position at a time. We recommend reviewing all available opportunities and applying to those that best match your experience and aspirations.
Benefits:
Salary:  £23,064
35 hours per week //  Half day Fridays! // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits!
About us:
Are you passionate about aviation innovation? Do you have a natural curiosity for problem-solving?
Quality Engineering is a vital transnational team within Airbus Commercial Aircraft. We ensure the highest quality assurance standards, driving the development of cutting-edge designs and technologies for both our new aircraft programs and existing product lines.
We collaborate closely with our engineering teams to ensure our products consistently meet all regulatory requirements, uphold stringent safety standards, and safeguard Airbus's global reputation.
An apprenticeship in Quality Engineering offers a unique opportunity to work across all Airbus Commercial Aircraft programs. You'll gain invaluable insights into the entire lifecycle of passenger aircraft, freighters, and private jets – from development and production to in-service processes. Starting your career in Quality Engineering provides a broad foundation, setting you up for excellent progression opportunities throughout Airbus.
Community & Culture
Being an engineering quality apprentice at Airbus means being part of a vibrant, supportive community. You will join an extensive apprentice network where you can share experiences and build lifelong professional connections. Beyond technical training, we provide dedicated support to guide your personal and professional growth, fostering a strong sense of belonging within our transnational team.
What you will be doing:
In this role, you will play a crucial part in our quality assurance mission, gaining the hands-on experience needed to launch your career in aerospace.
Right from the start of your apprenticeship, you'll gain hands-on experience by spending two days a week with our quality engineering teams at the Airbus facility in Filton (Bristol). For the remainder of the week, you'll attend Weston College (based at our site in Filton) to pursue an Engineering Manufacturing Technician Level 4 qualification.
From your second year onwards, your time at college will progressively decrease, allowing you to immerse yourself more fully in impactful projects and activities within the business.
Throughout your apprenticeship, you'll complete a variety of placements within quality engineering and related functions. You'll engage in crucial quality assurance activities such as:
• Root Cause Analysis: Investigating the underlying reasons for problems to ensure they are solved permanently, rather than just addressing the symptoms;
• Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA): Predicting potential risks or failures in designs or manufacturing processes to prevent them before they occur;
• Big Data Analysis: Interpreting large sets of information to spot trends, improve performance, and make data-driven decisions;
• Design Assurance: Validating that designs are developed correctly from the start to meet rigorous safety and regulatory standards;
• Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP): A structured framework used to ensure quality is built into the product development process from concept to delivery.
You will develop an excellent understanding of how quality engineering contributes to the successful design and delivery of modern commercial airliners. You will gain experience of working as part of a large multi-disciplinary transnational team engaged in the forefront of aerospace engineering. You will learn how to put into practice the latest quality methods and make use of the most modern digitalisation tools.
Requirements:
In order to be eligible to this apprenticeship, you must have a minimum of:
• ​A level in Maths and Physics at C or above
OR
• Level 3 engineering qualification (BTEC Level 3 Diploma/ Extended Diploma or T level) at Merit or above
AND
• Five GCSEs at 4/C and above including Mathematics, English Language and Science
Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate the following:
• A passion for working in a collaborative, team-oriented environment;
• An interest in finding creative solutions to complex problems;
• A commitment to acting with integrity;
• Persistence and resilience in the face of challenges;
• An inquisitive mind with a strong desire to learn and grow;
• High attention to detail;
• Submit your CV stating your grades and if they are predicted or achieved;
• Submit a Cover Letter highlighting your passion and suitability for this apprenticeship.
BOOST YOUR APPLICATION:
We want to get to know you—not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:
• Why Airbus and this apprenticeship?
What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? What is it about our company, our values, or the future of aerospace that excites you? We want to hear about what motivates you to pursue this unique path and how you see yourself growing with us.
• What skills and experience do you bring?
Think about projects, hobbies, or academic subjects that have given you practical experience. This could include personal projects, academic work and extracurricular activities.
Important Information:
GRADES: If you are on predicted grades, your offer will be conditional to achieving the position’s requirements before the apprenticeship start date.
SECURITY CLEARANCE: You will be subject to a BPSS (Baseline Personnel Security Standard) check. You may also need to gain UK SC-level Security Clearance or Export Control, depending on the role.
RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom for the full duration of the programme. For more information, please check the Government Website.
LEVY FUNDING: Successful candidates must be eligible for the levy funding.
Our apprenticeship roles do not meet the minimum requirements set by UK Visas & Immigration to enable sponsorship of migrant workers.

• Access to hundreds of high-street retailer discounts

A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
•
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
•
We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
•
We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond

Every day, around the globe, our imprints, books, journals, platforms and technology solutions reach millions of people. For over 175 years our brands and imprints have been a trusted source of knowledge to these communities and today, more than ever, we see it as our responsibility to ensure that fundamental knowledge can be found, verified, understood and used by our communities – enabling them to improve outcomes, make progress, and benefit the generations that follow.

We are looking for a Senior Laboratory Automation Specialist for a fixed-term contract to develop and deliver innovative laboratory automation solutions that enable science at scale at the Wellcome Sanger Institute. Working within the Technical Development and Scale-up team (TDS), you will lead complex projects from concept and technology evaluation through to validation and implementation. This is an opportunity to combine technical expertise in automated liquid handling and laboratory robotics with project leadership and scientific collaboration in a world-leading genomics research environment.
About the Role
You will lead the development and implementation of automated laboratory workflows, identifying where technology can improve scientific capability, efficiency and scalability. You will work across multi-functional teams and with external technology partners to turn complex requirements into robust solutions.
You will:
• Lead laboratory automation projects from concept through development, validation and implementation, balancing scientific requirements, cost, resources, timelines, quality and risk.
• Design and develop complex methods for automated liquid handling platforms, translating scientific protocols into robust, scalable workflows.
• Evaluate automation technologies and emerging solutions to identify the most appropriate approaches for scientific and operational requirements.
• Collaborate with faculty scientists, software developers and external partners to integrate new technologies, including integration with LIMS.
• Embed automated processes into Scientific Platforms, ensuring ongoing evaluation and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
• Share expertise by mentoring and supporting colleagues and contributing to a collaborative culture of innovation and shared learning.
About You
You will bring substantial hands-on laboratory automation experience and an ability to turn complex scientific requirements into effective automated solutions. Alongside your technical expertise, you will be comfortable leading projects, communicating with different audiences and collaborating across disciplines.
Essential criteria:
• Extensive experience of laboratory automation and automated liquid handling, including developing complex methods on platforms such as Hamilton, Agilent Bravo, Tecan, Beckman or comparable technologies.
• Experience of developing, validating and implementing complex automated or high-throughput laboratory workflows.
• Ability to evaluate liquid handling and automation technologies critically, using performance data and scientific requirements to inform decisions.
• Experience integrating laboratory automation with LIMS, and producing technical documentation such as SOPs and risk assessments.
• Strong project delivery, communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
• Knowledge of biological science gained through relevant study and/or equivalent practical laboratory experience.
• Experience in automating cell-based assays and/or molecular biological techniques.
• Background in cellular biology and cell culture techniques
• Background in Next Generation Sequencing (NGS), Long Read Sequencing technologies, & sample preparation
• Experience in automating NGS and long-read library preparation processes
• Proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous improvement
We recognise that relevant expertise can be developed in different environments. We welcome applicants from academia, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, diagnostics, technology development and other relevant sectors, and encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences.
About Us
The TDS team is part of Scientific Platforms at the Wellcome Sanger Institute. Our mission is to support cutting-edge research by developing and delivering high-throughput genomic and cellular technologies.
Our work enables researchers to explore fundamental biological questions, ranging from cancer genomics to biodiversity studies. The TDS Delivery team plays a vital role in piloting and implementing new Genomic & Cellular technologies into routine use, helping to maximise the efficiency, cost-effectiveness and quality of data generation across the Institute.

About Us
Druck is a global leader in high‑precision pressure sensing technology. Our products operate in safety‑critical environments across aerospace, industrial, and energy sectors. We pride ourselves on delivering high‑integrity, high‑reliability solutions for customers around the world.
We are now expanding our aerospace software capability and are seeking an Embedded Software Test Engineer to support the verification and validation of safety‑critical embedded software developed to DO‑178C Level A.
Role Overview
In this role, you will be a key contributor to the software verification and validation lifecycle, ensuring our embedded systems meet the highest aerospace safety and quality standards. You will work closely with software, and hardware engineers to design, execute, and document verification activities in line with regulatory and customer requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Software Verification Activities
• Develop and execute test plans, test procedures, and test cases to support DO‑178C qualification.
• Ensure all tests provide clear traceability to high‑ and low‑level requirements.
• Perform unit, integration, hardware‑in‑the‑loop (HIL), and system‑level testing of embedded software.
• Conduct debugging, problem investigation, and defect reporting, working closely with the software development team.
• Produce clear and accurate test reports, evidence packages, and certification documentation.
Compliance & Quality
• Perform verification activities aligned with DO‑178C, DO‑330, and the company quality management system (AS9100).
• Participate in reviews of requirements, architecture, and code to assess testability and completeness.
• Support structural coverage activities (including MC/DC) where required.
Technical Contribution
• Interpret hardware datasheets, microcontroller documentation, and interface specifications to develop robust and realistic test scenarios.
• Work with embedded toolchains, debuggers, simulators, and automated test environments as needed.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of test processes, tools, and templates.
Required Skills & Experience
Essential
• Proven experience in software verification and validation in an aerospace or safety‑critical environment.
• Hands‑on experience applying DO‑178B/C practices, ideally to Level‑A.
• Strong understanding of embedded systems and experience testing microcontroller‑based software and low‑level communication protocols.
• Ability to understand and assess C source code for testability (coding not required, but comprehension is).
• Ability to interpret hardware documentation and interface specifications.
• Must hold a British passport or have the right to work in the UK.
Desirable
• Experience with structural coverage (e.g., MC/DC using Parasoft ideally, but LDRA, VectorCAST, Cantata, etc. is also acceptable).
• Familiarity with requirements and configuration management tools (e.g., DOORS, GitHub).
• Experience with HIL/PIL test setups.
• Knowledge of tool qualification under DO‑330.
What You’ll Gain
• Opportunity to work on cutting‑edge aerospace technology.
• Growth in DO‑178C expertise and exposure to high‑integrity engineering practices.
• A collaborative team environment with experienced engineers.
• Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits.
Join Us
If you’re passionate about embedded systems, software testing, and high‑integrity engineering, we invite you to apply and grow your career with a globally respected engineering organisation.

Our team provides strategic planning and development advice to public and private sector clients, helping them maximise the potential of land and buildings. We are currently advising a diverse client base including banking, gov clients, investors.
This is an opportunity for a chartered or near-chartered Planner to take responsibility for their own instructions, work alongside senior colleagues on major projects and develop their client and commercial experience.
You will manage planning projects from initial advice through to submission and determination, while building relationships with clients, local authorities and other consultants.
As you develop in the role, you will also be expected to grow your internal and external network, identify new business opportunities and work with colleagues across Cushman & Wakefield to introduce clients to our wider real estate services.
Key Responsibilities
•
Prepare and submit planning applications, including Planning Statements and supporting documentation.
•
Prepare and manage planning appeals.
•
Manage planning instructions and projects on a day-to-day basis.
•
Provide clear planning advice directly to clients.
•
Undertake planning policy, site and development research.
•
Liaise and negotiate with local planning authorities and other stakeholders.
•
Attend client meetings, site visits and project meetings.
•
Attend public consultation events and planning committee meetings where required.
•
Support senior colleagues on large-scale and complex planning applications and appeals.
•
Coordinate with other professional disciplines and project consultants.
•
Manage existing client relationships and help identify opportunities for further work.
•
Develop relationships across the Midlands property market.
•
Work with other Cushman & Wakefield teams to identify cross-selling opportunities.
About You
You will have broad planning experience and the technical ability to manage smaller planning instructions independently, while contributing to larger and more complex projects.
You should be commercially minded, confident dealing directly with clients and interested in developing your network and career within the wider real estate sector.
We are looking for:
•
Around 2–3+ years' planning experience, ideally within consultancy or a similarly commercial environment.
•
MRTPI qualification, or someone close to achieving chartered status.
•
Ideally 1+ years' post-MRTPI experience.
•
An RTPI-accredited degree, ideally achieved at 2:1 or above.
•
Experience preparing and managing planning applications and appeals.
•
Experience managing projects and dealing directly with clients.
•
Good knowledge of the Birmingham and wider Midlands planning and development market.
•
Strong written, report-writing and verbal communication skills.
•
An understanding of business development and client relationship management.
•
Commercial awareness and an interest in the wider property and development market.
•
The confidence to analyse issues, provide solutions and take responsibility for your own workload.
•
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.
•
An ambitious and proactive approach, with an interest in taking on greater responsibility as your career develops.
•
A full driving licence.
•
Unrestricted right to work in the UK.
Why Cushman & Wakefield?
You'll join an established Land, Development & Planning team working on projects for major public and private sector clients, while benefiting from the wider expertise and client base of one of the world's leading real estate businesses.
The role offers exposure to a broad range of planning and development work, direct client responsibility and the opportunity to build your profile within the Birmingham and Midlands market.

About Waythrough
Waythrough was formed in 2024 following the merger of Humankind and Richmond Fellowship. Together, we’ve created one of the largest mental health and social support charities in England.
Every year, we support around 125,000 people through nearly 200 services – and it’s all made possible by our 3,500 brilliant staff and volunteers.
Make a real difference in your community
Are you passionate about helping others live safer, healthier, more independent lives? Join our team at Waythrough and support people facing challenges around mental health, substance use, housing or domestic abuse. This is more than just a job – it’s a chance to build meaningful relationships and create lasting change.
About the Role:
Our Floating Support Service provides flexible, person-centred support to individuals experiencing homelessness and challenges related to drug and alcohol misuse.
We work across community settings, supported accommodation, and outreach services to empower people to improve their wellbeing, sustain accommodation, reduce harm, and move towards greater independence.
The service supports adults with a range of complex and multiple needs, including substance misuse, mental health challenges, offending behaviour, and social isolation.
Our approach is recovery-focused, trauma-informed, and centred around building positive, trusting relationships that promote long-term stability and resilience.
What You’ll Do:
As a Floating Support Coordinator, you’ll play a key role in supporting individuals to:
• Maintain and sustain their accommodation and reduce the risk of homelessness.
• Develop independent living skills, confidence, and personal resilience.
• Access housing, benefits, healthcare, treatment services, education, training, and employment opportunities.
• Improve wellbeing through tailored support planning and practical assistance.
• Reduce harm and engage positively with recovery-focused services relating to drug and alcohol use.
• Build positive routines and strengthen connections within their local community.
You’ll provide flexible support through home visits, outreach work, welfare checks, and partnership working with a range of external agencies.
You’ll work both independently and as part of a supportive team, ensuring individuals receive compassionate, person-centred support that reflects their unique needs and goals.
To Succeed in This Role, You’ll Need:
We are looking for someone who is compassionate, motivated, and committed to supporting individuals with complex needs to achieve positive outcomes.
You’ll ideally have:
• Experience working with individuals affected by homelessness, substance misuse, mental health challenges, or social exclusion.
• An understanding of safeguarding, risk management, and recovery-focused support approaches.
• The ability to build positive professional relationships and maintain appropriate boundaries.
• Strong communication, organisational, and record-keeping skills.
• Confidence working independently in community and outreach-based settings, as well as collaboratively within a wider team.
• A flexible and proactive approach to supporting individuals with varying levels of need.
• A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle are essential, as the role involves travelling across the community to carry out home visits, outreach work, and appointments with service users.
Experience in support work or housing-related services is desirable, although we welcome applicants with transferable skills, relevant lived experience, and a genuine passion for helping others make positive changes in their lives.

• Plan, perform and review testing of IT general controls (ITGCs), application controls and information produced by the entity, and link IT risks to risks of material misstatement

• A good understanding of the UK regulatory environment, including the FCA and the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA)

• CASS and safeguarding assurance experience
• SOC 1/ISAE 3402 reporting experience
• Experience of fintech, payments, crypto or digital assets

You’ll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring. The things that set you apart, we value them, and you’re free to bring your whole self to work.

Life is more than work. We’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles and we’ll always do our best to keep work and life in balance.
Your impact here goes beyond your day job. From secondments to fundraising for local charities, you’ll be giving back to society. That drive to do the right thing runs through everything we do, grounded in our values: purposefully driven, actively curious, and candid but kind.

The Role
The Hiscox Portfolio Solutions (HPS) Claims and Delegated Manager is a unique new opportunity to manage modern and forward-looking books of claims. HPS comprises new distribution methods of placement going from lead Lloyd’s business with bespoke claims solutions to fast follow books.

This new division consists of four distinct but complementary teams:
• Alternative Risk – Written within Hiscox London Market since 2015, the team selectively backs a diverse range of underwriting expertise targeting new and developing profitable segments of the market.
• Beta-Follow – Supporting select broker cross-class follow facilities to create a diversified portfolio of risk operating through efficient underwriting and claims models.

• Structured Solutions – Focusing on multi-year and/or multi-line polices where traditional insurance solutions cannot meet a client’s individual needs.

As the use of data and advanced analytics blends with more traditional underwriting skills, however, there are significant opportunities to deliver innovative insurance solutions in key areas where clients might be looking for alternatives to traditional risk transfer, as well as to support data-led delegated authorities where Hiscox can provide significant insurance capacity.

• Managing the portfolios of claims for both lead, follow and fully delegated books of business.
• Liaising with Claims Operations and the Claims Vendor team to ensure appropriate claims processing structures are in place to support an efficient claims operating model and that claims data is readily available.
• Review and understand claims data to be able to provide insights into HPS books of business at a portfolio level. This will include identifying claims trends and activity that might require further investigation or action.
• Liaising with Reserving and Underwriting to review HPS books of business to ensure the claims performance of the books are well understood in order to support changes in pricing assumptions, underwriting appetite or reserving assumptions.

Person specification

• Be open to new ideas and new ways of doing things while having a firm grounding in the controls around claims both from within Hiscox and Lloyd’s.
• Have experience of overseeing a portfolio of claims across multiple lines of insurance business including both first party and third party especially in the Lloyd’s market.

Your role
You’ll be part of a busy, fast-paced Motor Claims department, supporting customers after a road traffic accident, regardless of fault. You’ll manage write-off claims from confirmation through to settlement, explaining vehicle valuations and next steps in a clear, straightforward way.
For many customers, losing their vehicle can be stressful. You’ll take ownership of their journey, listen to what matters to them and keep the claim moving. You’ll confirm the total loss, arrange settlement with the policyholder and organise disposal of the vehicle, while working with colleagues and external partners to resolve any issues.

• Set clear expectations and provide regular updates, especially when a customer is without a vehicle or needs extra support.
• Arrange settlements with policyholders and coordinate the disposal of written-off vehicles.
• Listen carefully, handle questions or objections confidently and support customers who may disagree with a valuation.
• Maintain accurate records, reserves and a proactive diary system so every claim is reviewed at the right time.

You’ll thrive in this role if you enjoy helping people, can take ownership and are comfortable balancing several priorities. We’d love you to bring:
• Outstanding customer service and strong verbal and written communication skills.
• Empathy, patience and active listening, particularly when customers are dealing with an upsetting or uncertain situation.
• The confidence to lead conversations, negotiate and handle objections fairly.
• A proactive approach and the resilience to stay composed in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong organisation and the ability to prioritise your workload.
• High attention to detail and confidence using multiple systems while speaking with customers.

• Up to 5% annual discretionary bonus.

The Opportunity:
The Process Safety Manager – Europe serves as the regional subject matter expert and leader for process safety, major accident prevention, and hazardous materials risk management across European operations. This position is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving process safety programs that protect employees, contractors, communities, company assets, and the environment while ensuring compliance with applicable European, local country, and company requirements.
The role provides technical leadership and governance for process safety management (PSM), risk assessment, management of change (MOC), major hazard prevention programs, fire and explosion prevention, hazardous materials management, emergency preparedness, and process safety performance improvement initiatives. The Process Safety Manager partners closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and site leadership teams to identify, assess, and mitigate process safety risks.
As a key member of the global EHS organization, the Process Safety Manager ensures alignment with corporate process safety standards while supporting country-specific regulatory obligations including Seveso III Directive requirements and other European major accident prevention regulations. The position requires approximately 35% travel to support audits, risk assessments, incident investigations, project reviews, emergency preparedness exercises, and facility engagement activities across Europe.

Process Safety Leadership & Governance
• Provide strategic leadership for process safety management programs across European operations.
• Develop and implement regional process safety strategies aligned with corporate standards and business objectives.
• Establish and maintain process safety governance systems, expectations, and performance metrics.
• Promote a strong process safety culture through leadership engagement, employee involvement, and continuous improvement.
Regulatory Compliance & Major Accident Prevention
• Ensure compliance with applicable European, national, and local process safety and hazardous materials regulations.
• Provide technical expertise regarding Seveso III requirements and other major accident prevention regulations.
• Support facility compliance programs related to hazardous substances, fire protection, explosion prevention, and emergency planning.
• Interface with regulatory agencies and support inspections, audits, permitting activities, and regulatory submissions.

• Ensure timely completion and revalidation of hazard assessments.
• Develop risk reduction recommendations and monitor implementation of corrective actions.
• Evaluate process safety risks associated with existing and new operations.
Management of Change (MOC)
• Lead and oversee Management of Change processes for equipment, technology, process, organizational, and procedural changes.
• Evaluate proposed modifications for process safety risks and compliance impacts.
• Ensure appropriate technical review, approval, and documentation of changes.
• Verify implementation of risk mitigation actions before startup.

• Support safe integration of new technologies and operational processes.
Incident Investigation & Organizational Learning
• Lead investigations of significant process safety incidents, near misses, fires, explosions, chemical releases, and high-potential events.
• Apply structured root cause analysis methodologies to identify systemic causes.
• Develop corrective and preventive actions and monitor effectiveness.
• Share lessons learned across sites to strengthen organizational learning and risk reduction.

• Oversee programs related to combustible dusts, flammable liquids, reactive chemicals, compressed gases, and hazardous materials storage.
• Evaluate facility safeguards related to fire prevention, explosion protection, loss prevention, and emergency response.
• Support process safety requirements related to chemical handling, storage, segregation, and transportation.
Audit, Assurance & Continuous Improvement
• Develop and execute process safety audit programs for European facilities.
• Conduct site assessments to verify compliance with corporate and regulatory requirements.
• Track audit findings and facilitate closure of corrective actions.
• Benchmark industry best practices and recommend opportunities for performance improvement.
Mechanical Integrity & Operational Excellence
• Support development and oversight of mechanical integrity programs for critical process equipment.
• Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering teams to improve asset reliability and risk management.
• Review inspection, testing, preventive maintenance, and integrity management practices.
• Monitor performance indicators to identify emerging risks and opportunities.
Training & Workforce Development
• Develop and deliver process safety training programs for employees, contractors, engineers, supervisors, and site leaders.
• Coach facility teams on process safety principles, risk assessment methodologies, and regulatory requirements.
• Serve as a technical resource for process safety-related questions and problem solving.
Emergency Preparedness & Business Continuity
• Support emergency response planning and major incident preparedness activities.
• Participate in emergency drills, exercises, and crisis management initiatives.

• Assist facilities in strengthening resilience and business continuity planning.

• Electronics Engineering

• A passion for solving complex engineering problems.

Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.

To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for industrial placement students who want to be part of something extraordinary—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
Our placements are designed to help you apply your studies in a practical setting, develop your technical skills, and gain valuable insight into how our business operates.
Our Industrial Placement Programme
Our Industrial Placement Programme offers you the chance to spend a year with us, working on meaningful projects alongside subject matter experts, within multidisciplinary teams, and across the product lifecycle. You’ll receive a salary of £26,228, with coaching and support from a dedicated team to help you achieve both your placement objectives and personal development goals.
Successful completion of an Industrial Placement with Leonardo may also lead to an offer on our Graduate Development Programme.
During your placement, we encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience. This Opportunity is based in Luton.
What You'll Do
As an Industrial Placement Antenna Engineer, you'll join a team delivering world-leading Electronic Warfare capabilities that protect fast jets, UAVs, naval vessels and land platforms operating in some of the world's most demanding environments.
As part of our Antenna Engineering team, you'll support the development of high-performance antenna systems used within advanced Electronic Warfare solutions.
Your activities will include:
• Supporting the design and development of innovative antenna solutions for a range of defence platforms
• Using electromagnetic (EM) simulation tools to model and analyse antenna performance
• Supporting the development of antenna technologies operating at frequencies up to 40GHz and beyond
• Conducting laboratory testing, measurement and validation using specialist RF equipment and anechoic chamber facilities
• Analysing technical data and presenting findings to engineering teams and stakeholders
• Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to integrate antenna solutions into larger systems
• Contributing to technical documentation, design reviews and customer deliverables
Your Industrial Placement Project
Approximately 50% of your placement will be dedicated to a cohort-led Industrial Placement project. Working alongside other placement students from different engineering disciplines, you'll define, manage and deliver a substantial project from concept through to final presentation.
This experience will help you develop project management, leadership, teamwork and stakeholder engagement skills alongside your technical development.
What We're Looking For

• Electronic Engineering
• Electrical Engineering
• Physics or Applied Physics
• Engineering Physics
• Mathematics or Applied Mathematics
• Communications Engineering
• Space Engineering
• Robotics Engineering
• Computer Communication and Networks
• Cyber Security or related STEM disciplines
We'd also like to see:
• An interest in electromagnetics, RF systems, antenna design or communication systems
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

The Placement Experience
You'll benefit from:
• Hands-on experience on real engineering projects
• Mentoring from experienced engineers
• Technical and professional skills development
• A dedicated Industrial Placement cohort project
• Exposure to multiple engineering disciplines and technologies
• Opportunities to build your professional network across Leonardo
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, our teams are key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.

• Tailored perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.
For a full list of our company benefits please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/company-benefits

Excellent knowledge of UK GAAP / FRS102

An interest in our clients, with the ability to confidently discuss business challenges and needs

Extensive experience of using audit software and Microsoft packages

Project management experience
•
An interest in maintaining and developing your technical knowledge

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary - shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We have several exciting opportunities for Graduate Systems Engineers within our Customer Support and Service Solutions (CS3) line of business. CS3 operates across the UK, developing and delivering innovative support solutions and services that help our customers keep critical capabilities available wherever and whenever they are needed.
Systems Engineering in CS3 is varied, and your role will cover one or more of the following areas:
• Support Solution Design: Help to understand customer needs and develop the support solutions and services that enable complex equipment to remain available and effective throughout its life. This could involve requirements, modelling, analysis and conceptual design, including work associated with Typhoon and the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP).
• Technical Support: Develop hands-on engineering experience through the testing, investigation and repair of some of our in-service equipment across helicopters and fast jets. You could work with electronic-based systems and associated test equipment, while developing your understanding of how individual products and equipment contribute to the wider support system.
• CS3 Engineering Capability Development: Help us improve how we engineer and deliver support solutions across CS3. You could explore new technologies, analyse and visualise data, develop engineering methods and tools, or investigate new approaches that improve the services we provide to our customers.
You do not need to decide which of these areas is right for you before applying. During the application process, we'll explore your interests, strengths and aspirations with you to help identify where you could be the best fit.
We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals. Our 18-month Graduate Programme will give you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside experienced engineers and industry leaders, while building both your technical and professional skills.
You won't be expected to know everything when you join. As a Graduate Systems Engineer in CS3, you'll receive coaching and support from your team and our dedicated CS3 Early Careers Manager. As your knowledge, experience and confidence grow, you'll take on increasing technical responsibility and ownership. We will also support you through your preferred route towards professional registration and chartership, and you'll have opportunities to get involved in STEM activities with local schools.
This role can be based at either our Luton or Edinburgh site. It is likely to include some travel within the UK and potentially overseas, providing opportunities to work directly with our customers and gain an understanding of their operational environment. Leonardo also operates a Custom (hybrid) working model that allows employees to split their time between attending the workplace and working remotely, subject to the needs of the role, team and customer.
On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria.
What you'll do as a Graduate Systems Engineer (Customer Support)
Dependent on the specific role, you will have the opportunity to do a combination of the following:
• Use and develop your technical knowledge to investigate problems, generate ideas and contribute proactively within your team.
• Develop practical Systems Engineering skills in the design, development, integration and verification of complex systems and support solutions, while building your understanding of the processes and technologies involved.
• Apply your academic knowledge to real engineering challenges across the engineering lifecycle, learning to deliver high-quality technical work within agreed cost and schedule constraints.
• Work collaboratively with engineers and specialists from multiple disciplines, learning from their expertise and contributing your own ideas and perspectives.
• Work with customers and stakeholders to understand their needs, operational context and the problems they need us to solve.
• Help to capture, analyse and manage customer and stakeholder requirements, and understand how these influence the design and development of a solution.
• Use data analysis, modelling, visualisation and dashboards to support engineering decisions and communicate insights.
• Complete your work to a high standard and in accordance with appropriate engineering processes, procedures and standards.
• Identify opportunities to improve engineering processes, methods and tools, and contribute ideas for how we can work more effectively.
The exact activities will vary depending on the team and area you join, giving you the opportunity to develop a broad understanding of Systems Engineering while building your technical knowledge and practical experience.
What we need from you
You will need:

We are seeking a highly motivated and ambitious candidate to join the PerkinElmer OneSource Scientific Services team based at one of our customer sites in Stevenage, UK.

• Self-motivated and able to work under pressure to prioritize conflicting deadlines.

• Service orientated attitude combined with innovative thinking.
• Strong interpersonal skills; strong team player with customer satisfaction focus

Preferred Qualifications

Work with biohazards upon completion of blood borne pathogen surveillance.

Business Unit
Cloud & Smart Industries Group (CSIG) is responsible for promoting the company's cloud and industry Internet strategy. CSIG explores the interactions between users and industries to create innovative solutions for smart industries via technological advancements such as cloud, AI, and network security. While driving the digitalization of retail, medical, education, transportation and other industries, CSIG helps companies serve users in smarter ways, building a new ecosystem of intelligent industries that connect users and businesses.
What the Role Entails
Position Overview
Tencent Cloud is seeking an AI & LLM Solution Architect to accelerate the adoption of Tencent Cloud's enterprise AI platform across Europe. This customer-facing technical role combines solution architecture, customer engineering, and hands-on AI implementation to help enterprises design, build, deploy, and scale production-ready AI applications. Leveraging Tencent Cloud TokenHub—a unified AI platform providing access to leading Large Language Models (LLMs), AI Agents, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem—you will work closely with enterprise customers, Product, Engineering, Research, and Commercial teams to bridge business challenges with innovative AI solutions. Beyond solution delivery, you will serve as the technical bridge between customers and Tencent Cloud's AI product organization, translating real-world customer requirements into product enhancements while accelerating enterprise AI adoption. TokenHub provides enterprises and developers with a unified gateway to leading foundation models through a single API, together with enterprise-grade model management, inference, deployment, monitoring, and AI application capabilities. Product Link: https://www.tencentcloud.com/products/tokenhub?from_qcintl=topnav
Responsibilities
•
Partner with enterprise customers to understand business challenges, identify AI transformation opportunities, and design end-to-end AI and LLM solutions leveraging Tencent Cloud TokenHub, leading foundation models, AI Agents, MCP ecosystem, and enterprise AI capabilities.
•
Lead technical discovery workshops, architecture design sessions, Proof-of-Concepts (POCs), technical validation, and production deployment planning to accelerate enterprise AI adoption.
•
Work directly with customer engineering teams throughout implementation and production rollout, troubleshooting complex technical issues and optimizing AI application performance within enterprise production environments.
•
Design scalable enterprise AI architectures utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs), Prompt Engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI Agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP), model fine-tuning, inference optimization, vector databases, API integration, AI workflow orchestration, and cloud-native AI services.
•
Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Research teams to translate customer requirements into platform enhancements, improve developer experience, and continuously evolve Tencent Cloud's AI platform through customer-driven feedback.
•
Develop reusable reference architectures, implementation frameworks, sample applications, technical playbooks, and best practices that accelerate enterprise AI adoption across European customers and partners.
•
Support strategic enterprise opportunities by leading technical proposals, architecture reviews, executive presentations, tender responses, and technical due diligence throughout the customer lifecycle.
Who We Look For
•
Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
•
Minimum 2 years of experience in Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), machine learning, AI platforms, cloud computing, software engineering, MLOps, solution architecture, or customer-facing technical consulting.
•
Hands-on experience with modern AI technologies including LLMs, Prompt Engineering, RAG, AI Agents, MCP, model fine-tuning, inference optimization, vector databases, AI orchestration frameworks, API integration, and cloud-native AI architectures.
•
Experience developing or deploying enterprise AI applications on public cloud platforms, with practical knowledge of multi-model AI orchestration, model deployment, inference services, observability, and production operations.
•
Strong customer-facing communication, presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex business requirements into scalable AI solutions.
•
Excellent written and spoken English is required. Proficiency in Chinese Mandarin is required to collaborate with China headquarters on product discussions, technical design, and cross-functional initiatives.
•
Self-driven with strong learning agility, curiosity for emerging AI technologies, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced customer-facing environment.

We are Rolls-Royce SMR and we’re doing something that’s never been done before. We’re revolutionising an industry. That’s a once‑in‑a‑career opportunity for those excited by such a challenge. This is more than just a job; this is a legacy.
The Electrical Systems team is responsible for delivering safe, resilient and technically robust electrical infrastructure across the Rolls‑Royce SMR power station. Earthing and lightning protection systems are fundamental to ensuring plant safety, regulatory compliance and system integrity. This includes the design, verification and substantiation of systems that protect both people and equipment, ensuring a consistent and compliant approach across the station.

As a Lead Electrical Engineer – Earthing, you will provide technical expertise across the design and development lifecycle of earthing and lightning protection systems. You will lead system architecture, sub‑system design, equipment specification and the selection of components necessary to realise the final verified design of the SMR power station.
You will work across engineering teams—electrical, civil, systems, safety and project functions—to ensure earthing systems are integrated effectively, compliant with UK and international standards and aligned with overall plant architecture. You will act as a responsible designer and intelligent customer, ensuring quality, consistency and technical rigour throughout the project lifecycle.
You will support design reviews, risk assessments, strategic planning, and technical governance activities. You may also mentor less experienced engineers and support engagement with suppliers, customers, regulators and external stakeholders.

• Provide technical leadership for earthing and lightning protection systems
• Assess and substantiate designs to ensure compliance with UK and international standards
• Develop system architecture, specifications, design documentation and component selections

• Lead or contribute to technical reviews, ensuring quality is maintained through project gates
• Identify risks and develop mitigations during system design and integration
• Support capacity planning, long‑term strategy and team development
• Work across power station engineering teams to deliver standardised, commoditised approaches to system design
• Represent electrical engineering in working groups, supplier engagements, customer discussions and regulatory dialogue
• Manage or oversee supply chain partners delivering work packages
• Coach and mentor less experienced engineers across the electrical discipline

• Knowledge of relevant earthing and lightning protection codes and standards for the UK and Europe
• Experience developing earthing and lightning protection systems in nuclear or high‑integrity environments
• Knowledge of systems engineering methodologies, including MBSE tools such as Capella, DOORS or Polarion
• Proven ability to manage contract partners delivering technical work packages
• Understanding of commercial availability and cost considerations for materials

The Customer Onsite Support Specialist supports patient safety at the customer site and acts as the interface between Haemonetics and the customer team. The role ensures that the BloodTrack system is deployed and functioning optimally, that issues are resolved promptly, and that service improvements are communicated, agreed and actioned appropriately.
Key Responsibilities
• Maintain the optimal functionality of the BloodTrack system, ensuring that hardware and software issues are identified, accurately diagnosed, recorded and actively resolved.

• Deliver operational BloodTrack Tx, blood fridge and remote issue training, including competency assessments, for relevant customer staff such as nurses, doctors, porters and agency colleagues.

• Deliver train-the-trainer sessions and advanced troubleshooting and hardware maintenance training for link nurses.
• Maintain training databases and ensure training equipment and approved materials are available when required.
• Create and update training slides, supporting documentation, posters, memos and other educational tools with customer input and approval.
• Keep clinical training materials aligned with current hardware and software, including up-to-date screenshots and clearly illustrated safety-critical steps.
Education and Experience Requirements
• Relevant professional background as a Biomedical Scientist, Pathology IT specialist, laboratory professional or Transfusion Practitioner.
• At least 5 years of experience in a nursing or clinical environment, with experience using clinical software applications.
• Clinical knowledge and practical experience sufficient to understand the context in which the products are used.
• Previous experience delivering training, coaching or competency assessments, ideally within a clinical or healthcare environment.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with attentive listening and the ability to adapt to clinical and technical audiences.
• Excellent organisation and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
• A high level of accuracy, including when working under pressure, and the ability to maintain confidential information.
• Sound judgement, practical decision-making and a proactive approach to resolving issues.
• Ability to build effective customer relationships and collaborate across clinical, technical and commercial stakeholders.
• A service-focused mindset and determination to deliver reliable support in a patient-safety-critical environment.
• Full driving license.
​
Working Arrangements
• This position is based at the customer site in Oxford, United Kingdom.
• Onsite presence is required five days per week.

Turn Data into Real Business Impact

Job Title: Software Engineer

As a Software Engineer in the Cloud UE (Unified Engineering) team, you will help design, build, and operate the services and streaming environments that deliver AVEVA's Unified Engineering products to customers as a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform on Amazon Web Services (AWS).
You will work across serverless APIs, identity and access flows, Windows-centric infrastructure, and desktop streaming technologies. You will contribute to CI/CD and infrastructure automation, champion security and compliance, and support service reliability and performance. As you gain experience, there may be an opportunity to join the team’s on-call rotation in the future, with full mentoring and support.
This is a role for someone early in their career who is eager to learn, proactive by nature, and excited by the opportunity to work across a broad and modern technology stack in a team that truly owns what it builds. You won't be expected to know everything from day one, but you will be expected to have the curiosity, drive, and resilience to grow quickly.
Key responsibilities
•
Build scalable AWS SaaS services: contribute to the design, development, and support of highly available platform components.
•
Develop integrations and serverless capabilities: deliver and maintain APIs (API Gateway/Lambda), event-driven workflows, and identity/SCIM integrations with AVEVA CONNECT.
•
Operate and improve cloud environments: support desktop streaming (Amazon WorkSpaces Applications) and Windows-centric infrastructure (EC2, FSx, Active Directory, DynamoDB) with strong observability and cost/performance focus.
•
Deliver securely with automation and teamwork: write clean, tested, documented, deployable code; contribute to CI/CD and infrastructure automation (Azure Pipelines, CloudFormation, Step Functions); collaborate in agile planning, troubleshoot issues, communicate risks, and continuously learn.
Essential requirements
•
Proactive, self-starting, and ownership-driven — takes initiative and cares about quality and production behaviour.
•
Curious and growth-minded — eager to learn new technologies, approaches, and continuously improve.
•
Able to work independently in a distributed team — manages time well, operates autonomously, stays accountable.
•
Resilient, collaborative communicator — positive with challenges, asks questions, shares knowledge, and communicates clearly in writing and verbally.
Desired skills and competencies
•
AWS & cloud foundations: VPC, EC2, S3, IAM/security groups; plus awareness of serverless (API Gateway/Lambda/DynamoDB), containers (Docker/ECS), and monitoring (CloudWatch/Datadog).

Software engineering & languages: practical development experience in C# and JavaScript/TypeScript (Angular/Node.js), comfortable working across multiple languages, with solid Git-based workflows.
•
DevOps & delivery: understanding of CI/CD principles and tools (e.g., Azure Pipelines) and infrastructure automation/IaC (CloudFormation, Terraform or similar).
•
Windows & security fundamentals: Windows administration (AD, Group Policy, PowerShell, enterprise deployment/packaging awareness) and security best practices (SSO/SCIM, least privilege, encryption, network segmentation).

Our global team of 2000+ developers work on an incredibly diverse portfolio of over 75 industrial automation and engineering products, which cover everything from data management to 3D design. AI and cloud are at the centre of our strategy, and we have over 150 patents to our name.

• Managing candidate relationships throughout the entire life cycle of the search and keeping the Consultant abreast of candidate updates.

• Demonstrating self-awareness, humility, empathy, and open-mindedness in the workplace.

Being a Propulsion Manufacturing Technician Craft Apprentice at Airbus means you will get to develop both Mechanical and Electrical skills within our programme. You will be immersed in a stimulating Manufacturing environment.
This apprenticeship offers a unique opportunity to launch your career in the fascinating world of space propulsion. As a Propulsion Manufacturing Technician Apprentice, you'll be part of a team that builds cutting-edge propulsion systems for satellites and spacecraft. You'll gain hands-on experience in a supportive and innovative environment, contributing to projects that push the boundaries of technology.
This programme is perfect for those with a passion for both mechanical and electrical precision, a knack for problem-solving, and a keen interest in seeing their work take flight. Join us in shaping the future of space exploration!)
What you will be doing
Year 1: You will study towards a Level 2 Engineering Operative ST0537 on the mechanical/electrical pathways, gaining both academic knowledge and practical experience.
Year 2: During the Apprenticeship you will have a unique opportunity to experience our Propulsion Production area of the business which will provide you with a comprehensive understanding of how a Satellite is manufactured at Airbus Defence & Space.
This includes working in small teams or on a one-to-one basis to manufacture Spacecraft Propulsion systems using the latest approved processes and advanced production techniques for Satellite manufacture.
Your key activities & responsibilities will be:
Mechanical Assembly
• Use of various different adhesives and bonding methods
• Use of hand measuring tools to meet tight tolerances
• Installation of various components to satellite structures
• Installation of various connector brackets
• Bonding of Heater Mats, Thermocouples and Thermostats to various surfaces
• Following process and tolerances to drawings on 3DX
Orbital Welding
• Use our state-of-the-art Orbital Welding Machines to weld together Propulsion Systems into sub-assemblies before welding the sub-assemblies together on the full Satellite Structure.
• Learn how to bend, shape and cut both Titanium and Stainless-Steel pipework to form the Propulsion System.
Electrical
• Learn various Electrical Techniques such as Crimping, Splicing, Soldering and Forming of Harnesses.
• Installation of Electrical Components such as Latch Valves, Pressure Transducers and Thrusters using End to End Harness Installation.
• Wire and route Harnesses for Heater Mats, Thermocouples and Thermostats

Job Description:
About Us
Flui Technologies is a leading software solution provider to the energy and water sector, delivering innovative and scalable software infrastructure and services since 1990. Our solutions - MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC adapter - support market competition, smart metering, network flexibility and supplier integration across Energy Retail, Energy Networks and Water Retail, and are used to manage messaging for more than 35 million electricity and gas meter points, with millions of records processed per day.
As the utility sector evolves to meet the challenges of Net Zero, Smart Metering, Energy Code reform, Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement, Demand-side Response and Embedded Generation, we combine deep industry knowledge with technical innovation to deliver robust, business-focused solutions backed by dedicated people and exceptional support. We are certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, reflecting our commitment to protecting data and managing risk.
The Role
The Head of Cloud Platform Engineering owns the operations and component-level architecture of Flui's AWS cloud estate - the infrastructure that underpins software processing critical market and metering data at national scale. This is a hands-on role: you will design, build and run cloud-native platforms combining AWS-native services with open-source components, and carry end-to-end accountability for how that estate performs, costs, and stands up to scrutiny.
Beyond architecture and operations, you will own FinOps and security for the cloud estate, and act as the accountable owner for its overall fitness for purpose - resilience, performance and scalability - as Flui's platforms scale to support a growing and increasingly complex utility market. You will work closely with the engineering leadership to ensure architecture decisions serve both the product roadmap and the operational realities of running critical infrastructure.
The role suits someone who wants to remain genuinely hands-on with design and build, while holding single-point accountability for how well the cloud estate is run, secured and paid for.
Job Responsibilities
The Head of Cloud Platform Engineering will report to the Technology Director and will be responsible for:
•
Owning the component-level architecture of Flui's AWS cloud estate, spanning AWS-native services and open-source/self-managed components (e.g. container orchestration, messaging, data stores, observability tooling).
•
Operating and continuously improving the platforms underpinning MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC adapter, with direct accountability for their resilience, performance and scalability at national-scale transaction volumes.
•
Designing and maintaining disaster recovery, high-availability and capacity plans appropriate to platforms supporting critical utility market infrastructure.
•
Owning FinOps for the cloud estate: cost visibility, forecasting, tagging and allocation, and driving measurable, ongoing cost optimisation without compromising reliability.
•
Owning cloud security posture: identity and access management, network security, encryption, vulnerability and patch management, and ensuring the estate operates in line with Flui's ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and wider compliance obligations.
•
Defining and maintaining the non-functional standards ('fitness for purpose') that platforms must meet - resilience, performance, scalability and observability - and holding engineering teams to them through architecture review and guardrails.
•
Remaining hands-on: designing, building and, where appropriate, personally implementing infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines and platform tooling alongside the wider engineering team.
•
Owning operational rigor for the estate - incident management, on-call practice, root-cause analysis and continuous improvement of SRE practices.
•
Making and owning build-vs-buy and AWS-native-vs-open-source decisions, balancing cost, control, operability and vendor lock-in.
•
Managing key vendor and technical relationships, including AWS itself and providers of critical open-source or commercial platform tooling.
•
Partnering with the product/engineering leadership to ensure cloud architecture decisions support the product roadmap and time-to-market, and recruiting/developing a small, high-calibre platform engineering team as the estate grows.
•
Championing knowledge sharing and technical education across engineering - documenting architecture decisions and standards, running internal sessions on cloud and platform practice, and mentoring engineers and technical colleagues to raise the wider team's capability.
Essential Competencies and Experience
Business Acumen
•
Demonstrable experience owning cloud platforms supporting a regulated, high-availability or critical-infrastructure business.
•
Ability to balance technical excellence with commercial and operational reality - cost, risk, and delivery pace.
•
Understanding of the utility/energy sector's data and resilience expectations is an advantage.
Cloud Architecture & Platform Engineering
•
Deep, hands-on AWS expertise across compute, storage, networking, data and security services, ideally evidenced by current AWS certification(s).
•
Proven experience designing and operating cloud-native platforms that combine AWS-native services with open-source components (e.g. Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka or equivalent messaging, Prometheus/Grafana or equivalent observability).
•
Track record of owning a FinOps practice and delivering demonstrable, sustained cloud cost savings.
•
Strong cloud security background - IAM, encryption, vulnerability management - and familiarity with compliance frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001.
•
Experience defining and meeting non-functional requirements: high availability, disaster recovery, performance/load testing and scalability at production scale.
General

Strong infrastructure-as-code skills (Terraform, CloudFormation or CDK) and mature CI/CD practice.
•
Comfortable operating hands-on day to day while also owning strategy, standards and team development.
•
A track record of sharing knowledge and raising technical capability across a team or wider engineering community - through documentation, mentoring, or internal training.
•
Willingness to participate in on-call/incident response as needed for platforms supporting critical services.
Job Qualifications

Your Personal Characteristics Will Include

Security and cost-conscious by default, without losing sight of reliability and delivery speed.

Job Description:
Technical Manager AI Consultancy
NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.
We’re happy to talk flexible working and consider reduced hours and job shares, we’ll support you to balance your work and life.
A look into the role
Knowing you’re right for us
We’ve set ambitious growth targets for the firm, and we need the right people to help us achieve these. We’re looking for people who will bring ambition and drive to their role. In changing markets, we need to be able to work at pace and be adaptable to change and to be curious, asking questions of ourselves, each other and our clients to ensure we are delivering the services and quality we expect.
As a technical Manager in our AI consultancy team, you will turn AI ideas into working solutions. You will work closely with clients, listening to their problems and agreeing what to build, but you will spend much of your time hands-on: building proofs of concept (early trials of AI ideas), writing code and guiding the next steps towards a live service.
You will also coordinate technical delivery teams from partner companies and other Grant Thornton firms, either embedded in teams or in some cases, leading them. We expect you to use Claude Code, Claude and other AI tools every day to build faster and to a higher standard, and to check carefully everything they produce.
Key responsibilities
Building and running proofs of concept
• Build working proofs of concept quickly, writing code yourself and using AI coding tools such as Claude Code
• Agree with clients what a proof of concept must show and how success will be judged
• Test results honestly, and explain clearly what worked, what did not and what it means
• Demonstrate your work and present findings to client teams in plain English
Going beyond the proof of concept
• Have a clear view of the path to live: the steps from a working trial to a secure, supported service that people use every day
• Build, or guide the building of, solutions to a standard that can grow beyond the trial
• Apply DevSecOps (building security into how software is built, tested and released) in your own work and in the work you review
• Keep cloud running costs visible and under control, following FinOps practice (managing the cost of cloud services)
Working with partner and delivery teams
• Coordinate technical delivery teams from partner companies and other Grant Thornton firms, agreeing clear roles, standards and ways of working
• Review their code, designs and results, and give clear, constructive feedback
• Work as an equal partner or in some cases, lead colleagues in every location and organisation
• Keep work on track for scope, timing, quality and budget, and raise risks early
Working with clients
• Run interviews and workshops with client teams to understand their problems, their data and how ready they are for AI
• Turn what you hear into clear technical options and sensible recommendations
• Explain technical choices simply to non-technical audiences
• Support senior colleagues with proposals, pitches and follow-up conversations
Producing high-quality work with AI tools
• Use Claude Code, Claude, Claude Design, Claude Cowork and other tools to write code, tests, documents, diagrams and client materials
• Check all AI-assisted work carefully for accuracy, security and quality before it reaches a client
• Share good practice, prompts and reusable code with the wider team
Responsible AI and risk
• Make sure solutions follow responsible AI principles, data protection law (including the UK General Data Protection Regulation, or UK GDPR) and sensible checks on how AI models are used and monitored
• Use only firm-approved tools when working with client information, and follow firm and client rules on how data is handled
• Keep code, client data and access details secure at all times
Joining us as a Technical Manager, the minimum criteria you’ll need is a degree in a technical subject, or equivalent professional experience and experience in building technology or AI solutions. It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
Essential
• Proven experience in building technology or AI solutions, in a consulting, technology or similar client-facing setting
• Hands-on coding skills, for example in Python, and experience building working prototypes quickly
• Regular, practical use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code to write, test and review code
• A good understanding of how large language models (the technology behind tools such as Claude) work, what they can and cannot do, and how to build useful solutions with them, for example by connecting them to a client’s own information
• Working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider (Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services or Google Cloud)
• A practical view of what it takes to move from proof of concept to live: testing, security, monitoring, support and cost
• An understanding of DevSecOps and FinOps principles
• Experience working with, or coordinating, technical teams in other organisations or locations
• Strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to explain technical ideas simply to non-technical people
• Good client skills, including listening, asking the right questions and building trust
Desirable
• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted building tools such as Cursor and Lovable
• Experience with AI agents (AI that can carry out tasks with limited supervision) and with connecting them to company systems
• Experience setting up automated testing and release processes
• Familiarity with data platforms and data governance
• Knowledge of AI regulation and responsible AI frameworks
• Experience with clients in financial services, private equity, the public sector or the mid-market
• Experience supporting bids and proposals
Tools
You will be expected to work confidently with Claude Code and other AI coding tools as we bring them into the team, alongside Claude, Claude Design, Claude Cowork and the Microsoft 365 suite. Experience with tools such as Cursor and Lovable is useful. Which tools you can use on client work depends on firm…

• Understanding of single security risk models and portfolio risk & return methodologies

Skills:

• Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and an ability to navigate the analytics platform for conducting analysis and deriving solutions
• Enthusiasm for, and comfort with, working in a high pressure and fast-paced environment with entrepreneurial and team-oriented setting
