Senior AI Platform Engineer
The Senior AI Platform Engineer is responsible for defining and delivering the infrastructure strategy underpinning IQVIA's Large Language Model (LLM) programmes. This role provides technical leadership across compute, data, model lifecycle management, evaluation frameworks, and platform engineering, ensuring research innovations can be successfully transformed into secure, scalable, and production-ready AI solutions.
Acting as a key technical leader and cross-functional integrator, the Senior AI Platform Engineer partners with research, product, infrastructure, data engineering, and MLOps teams to design and operate the platforms required to train, evaluate, deploy, and govern large-scale AI systems across IQVIA products and healthcare use cases.
Key Responsibilities
• Own the AI platform and infrastructure roadmap, leading the planning and execution of LLM initiatives and translating research requirements into scalable engineering solutions.
• Partner with centralised infrastructure teams to design and deliver high-performance compute environments across AWS and on-premises platforms, including GPU infrastructure, Slurm clusters, and migration from ad hoc research workflows.
• Optimise LLM training and inference workloads, supporting research and product teams in maximising performance, scalability, and reliability across the infrastructure stack.
• Establish and maintain model and data lifecycle capabilities, including dataset versioning, lineage tracking, reproducibility standards, and integration with model registries.
• Lead the evolution of knowledge graph infrastructure, driving technology selection, migration strategies, performance optimisation, and integration with AI workflows.
• Serve as the primary technical coordination point across AI Research, Data Engineering, MLOps, Product, and Infrastructure teams, resolving dependencies and prioritising activities critical to delivery.
• Provide technical leadership for vendor selection, procurement, and technology partnerships, advising on compute architectures, GPU specifications, AI platforms, and integration approaches.
• Define platform engineering standards, governance, and best practices while mentoring engineers and promoting operational excellence across AI and platform teams.
Skills & Experience
• Significant experience designing, building, and operating large-scale AI, machine learning, or distributed computing platforms in enterprise environments.
• Deep understanding of LLM architectures and their interaction with GPU infrastructure, including CUDA, cuDNN, NCCL, kernel-level acceleration libraries, and distributed training frameworks such as PyTorch.
• Strong knowledge of distributed training and inference strategies, including tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism approaches.
• Experience optimising LLM inference workloads using technologies such as vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA NIM, SGLang, or similar high-performance serving frameworks.
• Expertise in model optimisation techniques including quantisation, mixed precision training and inference (FP8, GPTQ, AWQ, LoRA), and performance tuning for large-scale model deployment.
• Advanced experience profiling, troubleshooting, and optimising GPU workloads using tools such as NVIDIA Nsight, DCGM, and related ecosystem technologies.
• Strong background in AWS cloud services, high-performance computing, distributed systems, containerised environments, and infrastructure automation.
• Experience with workload orchestration technologies such as Slurm, Kubernetes, Ray, or equivalent distributed compute frameworks.
• Demonstrated success bridging research and production environments, enabling rapid experimentation while maintaining operational excellence, governance, security, and reliability.
• Proven ability to lead complex cross-functional initiatives, influence technical direction, and communicate effectively with engineering, research, product, and executive stakeholders.

You will have access to the most cutting-edge technology, the largest data sets, the best analytics tools and, in our opinion, some of the finest minds in the Healthcare industry.

Regardless of your role, we invite you to reimagine healthcare with us. You will have the opportunity to play an important part in helping our clients drive healthcare forward and ultimately improve human health outcomes.
It's an exciting time to join and reimagine what's possible in healthcare.

We believe that a work environment that embraces diversity will give us a competitive advantage in the global marketplace and enhance our success. We believe that an inclusive and respectful workplace culture fosters a sense of belonging among our employees, builds a stronger team, and allows individual employees the opportunity to maximize their personal potential.

We tackle the most complex problems in quantitative finance, by bringing scientific clarity to financial complexity.
From our London HQ, we unite world-class researchers and engineers in an environment that values deep exploration and methodical execution - because the best ideas take time to evolve.  Together we’re building a world-class platform to amplify our teams’ most powerful ideas.

Take the next step in your career.
The role
G-Research is a fast-growing, software-driven organisation where data is at the heart of everything we do.
We are looking for an experienced Database Platform Engineer to join our Data Services team. In this role, you will help design, build and operate the mission-critical database platforms that underpin research, a global platform and business operations
This role focuses on providing highly available, performant and secure data services. Our environment spans multiple database technologies - PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and CockroachDB - deployed across both on-premises infrastructure and the cloud (AWS).
The role is highly collaborative, working with research and engineering stakeholders to deliver performant, resilient and secure database services at scale. You will gain deep expertise in our database platforms, drive automation and operational excellence, and help evolve the platform to meet the growing needs of the business.
Key responsibilities of the role include:
•
Building, operating and scaling distributed database services across on-premises and AWS environments
•
Supporting large-scale deployments of PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL and CockroachDB, ensuring high availability, disaster recovery and performance
•
Contributing to the design and implementation of automation for database provisioning, upgrades, replication and monitoring using Python, Ansible and Terraform
•
Driving improvements in performance tuning, query optimisation, indexing strategies and storage design
•
Collaborating with application and research teams to design and deliver database solutions that meet demanding scalability and latency requirements
•
Participating in the out-of-hours rota to provide support for critical systems
•
Staying up to date with industry trends and emerging database technologies, helping evaluate their applicability
•
Defining SLAs, KPIs and monitoring strategies to ensure platform reliability, security and service excellence
•
Proactively identifying and resolving stability, security and capacity issues across the platform
Who are we looking for?
We are seeking a Database Platform Engineer with strong technical expertise in database systems, automation skills and a passion for solving complex infrastructure problems at scale.
The ideal candidate will have the following skills and experience:
•
Strong experience with relational database platforms, such as PostgreSQL, MSSQL Server, MySQL, CockroachDB or similar
•
Good understanding of database internals, including query execution, concurrency, replication, indexing and partitioning
•
Hands-on experience running databases at scale
•
Strong proficiency with Linux and Python for automation
•
Familiarity with infrastructure as code, including Terraform, Ansible, Jenkins, Dagger, ArgoCD or similar
•
Experience deploying and running services in containerised or Kubernetes environments
•
Understanding of AWS services relevant to data platforms, such as RDS, Aurora, S3, EC2 or EKS
•
Familiarity with modern observability stacks, such as Prometheus, Grafana, Elk or OTel
Desirable Skills:
•
Experience with cloud-native and distributed SQL database, such as Aurora, YugabyteDB or TiDB
•
Knowledge of data streaming and integration tools, including Kafka, Debezium and CDC pipelines
•
Experience with security and compliance in database environments, for example covering encryption, auditing and RBAC
•
Familiarity with DataOps practices and collaboration with Data Engineering teams

Highly competitive compensation plus annual discretionary bonus

Lunch provided (via Just Eat for Business) and dedicated barista bar

9% company pension contributions

Informal dress code and excellent work/life balance

Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer
Locations: DL, DH, NE, SR, TS
Are you a qualified Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer looking for excellent earning potential, structured work and the security of working directly for an established energy supplier?
At Utilita, we're growing our award-winning Field Services team. Join one of the UK's fastest-growing energy suppliers and a business that has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 Best Workplaces for four consecutive years.
What is in it for you?
You'll receive a base salary of £38,993, alongside uncapped earning potential and a variety of opportunities to boost your overall earnings, including:
• On-call payment: Receive £330 for each on-call week, based on an average rota of one week in five. (OTE of £42,293 just with the base salary and conducting mandatory on call requirements)
• Industry-leading installation bonus: Benefit from an uncapped installation bonus of £25 per meter or £50 per dual installation once you have completed a minimum of four installations in a day, with additional work opportunities available to further enhance your earnings.
• London weighting: Receive an additional £2,000 annual allowance if you live within the M25.
• Enhanced overtime: Enhanced overtime rates for Sunday working.
Alongside your salary and uncapped earning potential, you will receive 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, a healthcare scheme, mental wellbeing support, access to 24/7 GP and counselling services, and a generous pension scheme. You will also receive one paid volunteering day each year and have opportunities to win tickets to events at Utilita-sponsored arenas and football matches.
Why work at Utilita?
A schedule that supports your work-life balance.
We understand that a great Smart Meter Engineer role is not just about salary. It is also about having a structured working day and being able to plan your life accordingly.
You will be scheduled an average of 4 jobs per day, with an average travel time to jobs of approximately 35 minutes between appointments.
We aim to schedule your work several weeks in advance, giving you greater visibility of your schedule. This helps you plan life outside work while still giving you the opportunity to take on additional work when it suits you.
First-class training and support.
Your journey will begin at our award-winning training academy in Warrington, where you will receive a comprehensive induction.
You will then receive ongoing mentoring to help you strengthen your knowledge, understand our processes and confidently adapt to the Utilita way of working.
A team that keeps you connected.
We understand that working in the field can sometimes feel isolating, which is why creating a connected and supportive environment is so important to us.
Through regular manager check-ins, access to technical experts, collaborative colleague networks and ongoing communication, you'll always have the support you need and someone to turn to throughout your working day.
What you will be doing.
As a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer, you will represent Utilita in customers’ homes, installing smart meters safely and professionally across domestic properties.
You will play an important role in delivering our customer-first approach, providing a positive experience while maintaining high standards of safety, quality and service.
What we need from you.
To be considered for this opportunity, you will need:
• Smart Metering qualifications, including CCN1 or CMA1 and MET1, or equivalent.
• At least 12 months experience working as a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer.
• A valid full UK driving licence.
Who are Utilita?
Founded in 2003, Utilita Energy was created to challenge the Big Six energy suppliers by offering a fair and flexible service that is good for both the pocket and the planet.
As the first supplier to install a Smart Meter back in 2005 and kick-start Britain’s smart meter revolution, we continue to invest in smart technology and look for new ways to improve our services through innovation.
We are also committed to sustainability, with an ambition to become a Net Zero business by 2030. We believe everyone can make a meaningful impact through small, positive changes.
Our values are simple but powerful:
Fairness. Smart. Sustainability.
Our employees and customers come from all walks of life. We are committed to championing diversity, creating an inclusive culture and providing an environment where you can be your authentic self.
Utilita is part of the Luxion group which comprises Luxion Group Ltd, Utilita Energy Ltd, Luxion Sales Ltd, Utilita Field Services Ltd, Procode Technology Ltd and Canary Care Global Ltd.

JR034072
Glasgow
This is an Executive Director level position within our Accounting & Regulatory Policy Job Family which is responsible for the firms Accounting Policies under USGAAP and IFRS and Basel Based Regulatory Capital and Liquidity policy.
Accounting & Regulatory Policy ('Policy') is a global function within Finance which supports Morgan Stanley in achieving its business goals by providing independent, enterprise level advisory and oversight in relation to Accounting Policy and Prudential/Regulatory Policy for a broad range of internal and external stakeholders.
As a result of this focus, Policy plays a critical role in safeguarding the Firm's financial integrity, regulatory standing and risk profile, and in supporting strategic decision making across the Firm. Policy is a key contributor to client advisory, major Firm initiatives and regulatory change programs, helping to shape and influence the Firm's long term strategy.
Following a continued expansion in scope, complexity, and senior stakeholder engagement, an Executive Director opportunity has arisen within the Glasgow Accounting & Regulatory Policy team, which operates as a global centre of excellence and senior advisory hub for the Firm.
The role has global remit and accountability, with responsibility across Accounting and Regulatory Policy, including IFRS, US GAAP and Basel based frameworks. The role provides enterprise wide influence, advising leadership on matters with material financial, regulatory, and reputational impact.
What will you be doing?
Enterprise leadership and strategic impact
> Act as a senior leader within Policy, accountable for driving consistent, well governed policy outcomes across regions and legal entities.
> Provide strategic, forward looking advice to senior management on accounting and regulatory developments that may impact the Firm's financial position, capital, disclosures or strategy.
> Apply an enterprise risk lens to policy interpretation, ensuring alignment between accounting outcomes, regulatory expectations and the Firm's risk appetite and governance framework.
Accounting Policy
> Provide authoritative leadership on IFRS and US GAAP interpretation, with particular focus on complex, judgement heavy areas and issues with Firm wide impact.
> Own and oversee the Firm's global GAAP horizon scanning agenda, translating emerging standard setter developments into clear assessments of risk, impact, and recommended actions.
> Act as final escalation point within Glasgow Policy for complex accounting matters, including significant transactions, structural changes, and disclosure judgements with material financial or reputational consequences.
Regulatory Policy
> Provide senior policy leadership on prudential regulation, including Basel III, CRR/CRD, PRA rules, and related supervisory guidance, ensuring robust, defensible interpretations are applied consistently across the Firm.
> Advise on regulatory policy implications of strategic initiatives, balance sheet changes and evolving business models, focusing on capital, leverage, liquidity and regulatory disclosure impacts.
> Support the Firm's response to regulatory change by shaping policy positions, governance frameworks, and implementation approaches for high impact regulatory initiatives.
Firm initiatives and senior stakeholder engagement
> Represent Policy in major Firm programs, steering committees and governance forums, influencing outcomes where policy judgement is central to success.
> Serve as a trusted advisor and thought partner to senior stakeholders across Finance, Risk, Legal, Treasury, and the Businesses, exercising independent challenge where appropriate.
> Ensure complex issues are appropriately escalated, documented, and resolved in line with Firm governance expectations. Leadership & team development
> Provide visible, senior leadership within the Glasgow team, setting expectations aligned to Executive Director standards of judgement, ownership, and accountability.
> Manage and develop senior team members, with accountability for performance management, talent development, and succession planning.
> Drive sustainable capability building across Policy, ensuring the team is positioned to meet future accounting and regulatory challenges.
What we're looking for
> Qualified accountant (CA, CPA, ACCA or equivalent).
> Deep technical expertise in IFRS and/or US GAAP, combined with strong understanding of prudential regulatory frameworks and supervisory expectations.
> Proven experience providing senior level accounting and/or regulatory policy advice on issues with enterprise wide financial, regulatory, or reputational impact.
> Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgement in complex, ambiguous situations, balancing technical rigor with commercial and risk considerations.
> Strong influencing and communication skills, with the credibility to engage and challenge at Executive Director and Managing Director level.
Skills that will help you in the role
> Strategic mindset, with the ability to connect technical policy detail to Firm level outcomes.
> Strong appreciation of enterprise risk, governance and regulatory expectations.
> Experience contributing to or leading large scale accounting or regulatory change programs.
> Collaborative leadership style, combined with the confidence to challenge constructively and drive decisions.

Capital One is searching for an Incident and Problem Manager to join our UK Technology Operations Centre (TOC) team. The TOC is dedicated to the effective management, coordination, and communication of all major and critical incidents, as well as owning post-incident Root Cause Analysis.
This role is highly service-focused and requires close liaison with internal Technology teams, Business Partners, and real-time engagement with sourcing partners and suppliers to effectively manage major and critical Incidents and Problems impacting our business.
Initiatives such as Reliability Testing Game Days utilising Chaos experiments to maintain always-on Incident readiness across UK Tech in our operational and technical response will be a prominent feature of this role so relevant experience in these areas is preferable.
The successful candidate must have strong Incident Management experience, a Technology background and experience in utilising AI to remove TOIL and add value. Exceptional communication skills and the ability to display a flexible problem solving approach are essential.
The TOC is a 24*7*365 operation with online presence between 08:00-17:30 and on-call coverage providing out of hours support.
What you’ll do
• Lead Investigations: You will direct investigations into major and critical incidents by managing, coordinating, and appropriately challenging technical resources on a 24*7*365 basis.
• Drive Communications: Ensure that incident progress is continuously tracked via action plans and communicated effectively to the wider organisation.
• Coordinate Teams for Quick Resolution: Lead virtual and office-based support teams to ensure the restoration of normal service operations as rapidly as possible, keeping business disruption to a minimum.
• Rigorous Root Cause Analysis: Conduct investigations into root cause utilising 5 why’s methodology, while establishing actions to prevent recurrence and raise standards across Tech.
• Drive Incident Readiness: Greater service stability means fewer opportunities to prove tech resiliency and sharpen critical Incident behaviours. You’ll play a key role ensuring our people and Tech are always ready via Game Days in support of our Reliability Assurance agenda.
• Spearhead Process Improvement: Lead process and service improvement initiatives that align with your personal development objectives. This is your chance to embrace AI, as well as automate repetitive, manual incident and problem management tasks.
• Provide On-Call Support: You will perform on-call cover for Incident Management on rotation.

• An inquisitive and proactive mindset.
• Ability to communicate openly and effectively in both written and verbal form, with the confidence to meet effectively with external and internal Senior stakeholders.
• The ability to remain calm and focused in a pressured environment, carefully considering the needs of multiple stakeholders.
• An understanding of AWS Cloud technology principles. (Note: If you have advanced technical skills here, you will be highly empowered to drive automation!)
• Highly organised with an ability to remain focused and flexible when managing multiple initiatives
• Prior experience of using AI to drive process improvement initiatives that have added tangible value

This is a permanent position and is based in our Nottingham Head Office.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
Title:  Consultant - Cost-Evidence-Based Funder
Total number of Consultants: One (1)
Country Program: Best Use of Resources (BUR), Airbel Impact Lab, based out of USA, UK, or Kenya
Proposed Dates: 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027
Duration: Six months; 20 hours per week; approximately 520 hours in total.
Background of the project
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) engages a rapidly growing pool of cost-evidence-based funders, whose allocation decisions are primarily based on rigorous impact-per-dollar analysis. Historically, humanitarian programming has not been a focus of this funder community. However, in recent years, the IRC has increasingly received cost-evidence-based funder support for a wide range of initiatives, from conducting exploratory research to scaling malnutrition treatment to influencing foreign aid. As the “Solutions NGO”, cost-evidence-based funders represent a values- and results-aligned opportunity to increase the reach and cost-effectiveness of IRC’s programming.
This consultancy sits within the Best Use of Resources (BUR) team and reports to the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness. It is a time-limited engagement to support IRC’s relationships, value proposition and funding from cost-evidence-based funders, and to strengthen the BUR team’s own capability in the analysis these funders expect.
Scope of work
Working with the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness, and in deep collaboration with other IRC colleagues, the Consultant will produce materials that deepen and grow a portfolio of cost-evidence-based funder relationships, translate BUR’s cost-effectiveness research and IRC’s programming into donor-facing funding opportunities, and build IRC’s thought leadership profile within the community.
In consultation with the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness, the Consultant will determine the method and means of performing the work. The content of each deliverable will be agreed in advance with the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness, who will review and accept deliverables.

• Develop and apply novel computational methods for patient segmentation, biomarker discovery, and hypothesis generation from multimodal clinical and omics datasets, in partnership with Translational, Clinical, and Statistical Scientists
